attribution.note: Marcus's own list item in his own post, under his lead-in 'I seriously doubt AI will be able to do by the end of 2025'.

semantics.note: The proposition is faithful and keeps the 'seriously doubt' hedge, the 2025 horizon and the grounding qualifier. 'Seriously doubt' expresses graded improbability, not a firm commitment to the outcome.

contract.note: The contract scores the claim as a directional forecast on a plain reading. Policy allows plain-reading scoring only for firm language, and 'seriously doubt' is hedged. Terms like 'engaging', 'obvious' and 'representative' are also evaluator choices.

evidence.note: 2025 preprint with an automated composite biography score from a GPT-4o judge. It does not measure human engagement or obituaries.
2023 brief test by one reporter of an obituary tool. It predates the forecast and is anecdotal.

reviews.rationale: 'I seriously doubt' is graded, probabilistic language ('unlikely'), not an unqualified forecast, so policy says it is not scored. Even if it were scored, the packet has no joint factuality-and-engagement evaluation of both genres, so the result would be unresolved.

attribution.note: Marcus's own judgement of Musk's claim, written in his own post.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps 'if I understand it correctly' and 'almost certain'. Because the statement depends on Marcus's reading of Musk's claim, it is better classed as a conditional forecast. It also says 'AI' where Marcus wrote 'AGI', a minor difference.

contract.note: The contract treats Marcus's stated qualifier as an antecedent that must be established before scoring. That condition comes from the speaker's own words, though how Musk's intent is to be established is the evaluator's choice.

evidence.note: The host page confirms the interview date of 8 April 2024. It says nothing about the capability Musk meant.
Contemporaneous report of Musk's smartest-human prediction. It does not establish universal task coverage, and Mitchell's quote only shows that the comparison is ambiguous.

reviews.rationale: The contract requires independent evidence that Musk meant universal intellectual-task capability. Neither item establishes that, so the antecedent is unknown and policy says the claim is not scored. The packet also has no capability evidence for the end of 2025.

evidence.note: May 2025 benchmark showing models struggle with whole-game progress. It used earlier models and a stronger objective than the claim's.
December 2025 DeepMind report showing partial transfer to held-out games. It does not show rapid mastery across almost any game.
December 2025 NVIDIA report stating that the system cannot plan or follow instructions. It includes no timed evaluation on unfamiliar games.

reviews.rationale: 'I seriously doubt' is probabilistic language ('unlikely'), so policy says it is not scored. Even if it were scored, no item tests broad unfamiliar-game learning within minutes or hours, so the result would be unresolved.

attribution.note: Marcus states his own $1 million bet offer, made because he doubted Musk's prediction.

semantics.note: A wager that AGI superior to the smartest humans would not arrive by the end of 2025 is a firm, scored forecast. The proposition matches it.

contract.note: The contract uses Marcus's own threshold from the same post: one piece of intellectual work humans can do that AI can't. That reading is fair and ordinary.

evidence.note: Retrospective by the ARC Prize Foundation, published January 2026 (before the evaluation date). Every ARC-AGI-2 task was solved by untrained humans, while the top private-set score in 2025 was 24%.
On 5 December 2025, the best verified scores on human-solvable tasks were 37.6% (commercial model) and 54% (refinement system), so a clear gap remained.
Poetiq reported 75% on the public set on 23 December 2025. This is the company's own unverified claim, on a different split, and still well short of human coverage.

reviews.rationale: The deadline has passed. Independent ARC Prize evidence shows human-solvable reasoning tasks that the best late-2025 systems still failed, and even Poetiq's later self-reported 75% leaves a gap. No evidence shows a system meeting Marcus's bar by the end of 2025.
